convention: literal line-by-line, rules 1-7 of batch 05's brief
reasoning_summary:
Refrains fixed: 'O Hymenaeus Hymen, / O Hymen Hymenaeus' and 'O Hymen Hymenaeus io,' (io kept as the ritual cry); prodeas, nova nupta is always 'may you come forth, new bride'; the quis huic deo stanza tails are identical each time.
Names as printed: Vinia and Manilus (16, noted against Iunia/Manlius); Au-/runculeia split across 86-87 as in the Latin; Talasius (134), Torquatus, Telemachus with Penelopeo noted as an adjective.
Gap markers at 79-82 and 112-114 kept as '. . . . .' with notes; 83 and 115 flagged as constructionally uncertain after the gaps. Source misprint 'quac' (117) kept in the Latin, rendered as quae with a note.
Hyperbaton left split by line rather than repaired: niveo/pede (9-10), tuus ... vir and in mala ... adultera (101-102), teneris ... papillis (104-105), tuum/os (138-139), te ... neglegit (198-199), vestri ... ludi (209-210).
Relatives checked: quos = ramulis (23) and specus (29), quem = pudor (84), quod = cubile (111), quae neuter plural = gaudia (116), quae feminine = terra (71) and domus (158).
Metaphors literal with notes: comas 'hair' of torch flames (78, 99), flammeum 'bridal veil' (122), lusisti nucibus (133), munere 'service' (234). Coarse/sexual content plain: concubinus 'concubine' (the groom's male bedmate), glabris 'smooth ones' (boys), papillis 'little breasts'.
Uncertain words noted: dedis (present of dedo), parthenice (a white flower), cinerarius (hair-curler), male abstinere (abstain reluctantly), iuverit (perfect subjunctive or future perfect).
